title: en la costa atlántica de Colombia, un Twin Otter de la aerolínea Aces que volaba entre Montería y Coveñas, se estrella en un cerro. El accidente deja un balance de once muertos.
text: Aces fue una aerolínea colombiana con sede en la Torre del Café en el centro Medellín, Colombia.​ Fue fundada en 1971 y liquidada en 2003 tras fusionarse con Avianca.​

title: Liga colombiana: Atlético Nacional, campeón.
text: La División Mayor del Fútbol Colombiano es una entidad deportiva que forma parte de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol y se encarga de organizar, administrar y reglamentar los torneos de fútbol profesional en Colombia: Primera A; Primera B; la Copa Colombia, la Superliga de Colombia y la Liga Femenina.

title: Pantanal Matogrossense National Park designated in Brazil.
text: The Pantanal Matogrossense National Park is a national park in the state of Mato Grosso at the border to Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.

title: Publication of Stephen Jay Gould's critique of biological determinism, The Mismeasure of Man, in the United States.
text: Stephen Jay Gould was an American paleontologist, evolutionary biologist, historian of science, and one of the most widely read authors of popular science of his generation. Gould spent most of his career teaching at Harvard University and working at the American Museum of Natural History in New York.

title: The burning of Jaffna Public Library in Sri Lanka is begun by a mob of police and government-sponsored paramilitaries. They destroy over 97,000 volumes in one of the worst examples of ethnic book burning in the modern era.
text: A paramilitary is an armed, militarized-like force or unit that functions and is organized in a manner analogous to a military force, but does not have professional or legitimate status. The Oxford English Dictionary traces the use of the term "paramilitary" as far back as 1934.

title: Sefer ve Sefel opens as an English used bookstore in Jerusalem.
text: Sefer ve Sefel is an English-language secondhand bookshop in downtown Jerusalem, Israel. It was established in 1981 as the first combination bookshop/coffee shop in the country.

title: John Gardner successfully revives the James Bond novel series originated by Ian Fleming with Licence Renewed (not counting a faux biography of Bond and a pair of film novelizations, the first original Bond novel since 1968's Colonel Sun).…
text: Ian Lancaster Fleming was a British writer best known for his postwar James Bond series of spy novels. Fleming came from a wealthy family connected to the merchant bank Robert Fleming & Co., and his father Valentine Fleming was the Member of Parliament for Henley from 1910 until his death on the Western Front in 1917.

title: Colin MacCabe is denied tenure at the University of Cambridge, apparently because of a dispute within the English Faculty about the teaching of structuralism.
text: Colin Myles Joseph MacCabe is an English academic, literary critic, film scholar, author, and film producer. He is currently a distinguished professor of English and film at the University of Pittsburgh.

title: The PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction is given for the first time.
text: The PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction is awarded annually by the PEN/Faulkner Foundation to the authors of the year's best works of fiction by living Americans, Green Card holders or permanent residents. The winner receives US$15,000 and each of four runners-up receives US$5000.

title: Picasso's painting Guernica is returned from New York to Madrid.
text: Pablo Ruiz Picasso was a Spanish painter and sculptor who spent most of his adult life in France. One of the most influential artists of the 20th century, he is known for co-founding the Cubist movement, the invention of constructed sculpture, the co-invention of collage, and for the wide variety of styles that he helped develop and explore.

title: unknown date – Blek le Rat begins his stencil graffiti art in Paris.
text: Blek le Rat is a French graffiti artist. He was one of the first graffiti artists in Paris, and has been described as the "Father of stencil graffiti".
